You are a research assistant preparing a literature review on transformer architectures in natural language processing. Your goal is to collect papers from multiple academic sources, analyze them, organize them in a knowledge base, and produce a comprehensive review document.

Start by searching the scholarly database for papers related to "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers related to "attention mechanism" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Query the scholarly paper catalog through the scholarly MCP — its search-arxiv tool returns arXiv-style entries that include paper IDs, which you will need for the overlap analysis below. Retrieve all available papers and note their titles, authors, publication years, and journal references.

Next, search the arxiv repository (via the arxiv_local MCP) for papers about "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers about "neural network" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Download and read through the abstracts of the papers you find to understand what each paper covers.

Write and run a Python analysis script. The script should take the collected paper data and categorize each paper into one of these methodology categories: "Architecture Design" for papers proposing new model architectures, "Training Methods" for papers about training techniques or optimization, "Applications" for papers applying transformers to specific tasks, and "Survey" for papers that review or survey the field. Assign categories based on keywords in the title and abstract. The script should also identify which papers appear in both databases (overlap analysis by matching paper IDs).

Create a database in the knowledge base titled "Research Paper Tracker" with properties for Title (title type), Paper_ID (rich_text), Authors (rich_text), Year (number), Category (select with options Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey), Source (select with options Scholarly, Arxiv, Both), and Abstract_Summary (rich_text). Add a page entry for each unique paper found across both databases.

Create a Word document called Transformer_Literature_Review.docx in the workspace. The document should have a title "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP", followed by an introduction section explaining the scope of the review. Then include a section for each methodology category listing the papers in that category with their titles, authors, year, and a brief description from the abstract. End with a conclusion section summarizing the state of the field and identifying research gaps.

Create an Excel file called Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet "Paper_Catalog" should have columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Source (Scholarly, Arxiv, or Both), and Category. The second sheet "Method_Comparison" should have columns Category, Paper_Count, Avg_Year, and Key_Papers (listing titles of papers in that category). The third sheet "Citation_Matrix" should list all unique papers with columns Paper_ID, Title, In_Scholarly (Yes or No), In_Arxiv (Yes or No), and Overlap (Yes if in both, No otherwise). Write paper IDs as plain text (e.g. 1706.03762) and all other cell values as literal values — do not write Excel formulas.

Your workspace contains review_guidelines.json with category definitions and lit_review_template.md with formatting guidance.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves. The main agent first dynamically locates and reads review_guidelines.json and lit_review_template.md from the task-visible workspace.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly two source sub-agents in parallel:
1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): One explore sub-agent calls the Scholarly search-arxiv tool exactly twice, once for transformer and once for attention mechanism. It returns the complete responses available from those two calls, normalized arXiv-style paper IDs, titles, authors, years, journal references, abstracts, query membership, duplicate IDs, and missing-field controls. It is strictly read-only.
2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): One explore sub-agent owns the local-arXiv branch. It calls search_papers exactly twice for transformer and neural network with the service's largest safe result limit, deduplicates normalized IDs, then uses download_paper and read_paper for each unique result as needed to verify its abstract. It writes no final artifact; if the corpus is large, it persists one runtime-unique JSON in the discovered task workspace and returns only path/hash/counts plus compact metadata controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent reconciles IDs without losing source membership, then writes and runs the required Python analysis script. The script consumes the two verified corpora, unions by normalized Paper_ID, labels Source as Scholarly/Arxiv/Both, assigns exactly one of Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey from the guidelines and title/abstract evidence, and emits one canonical runtime JSON containing all unique papers, overlap flags, category counts, and controls. Read the script and JSON back before Wave 2.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly three coder sub-agents in parallel from that same canonical JSON:
1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the exact-title Notion database Research Paper Tracker. Fully paginate search before create/reuse, block on duplicate exact-title databases/pages, enforce Title, Paper_ID, Authors, Year, Category, Source, Abstract_Summary with exact types/options, upsert one page per Paper_ID, and query/read all managed pages back.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Transformer_Literature_Review.docx. Follow lit_review_template.md, use the exact title and category sections, cover every unique paper with abstract-grounded text, add evidence-based gaps, and read the document back.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx. Create exactly Paper_Catalog, Method_Comparison, Citation_Matrix; use plain-text IDs and literal values, preserve every source flag/category, and read all populated ranges back.

Each writer must self-correct before returning. The main agent compares only IDs, counts, categories, titles, years and overlap flags across the three receipts; no third wave or repair agent is allowed.

You are an academic-literature researcher (read-only) helping build a literature review corpus on transformer architectures in NLP.

GOAL: Collect paper metadata from the SCHOLARLY database (via the scholarly MCP) by making EXACTLY TWO calls to the mcp__scholarly__search-arxiv tool:
1. Call 1: keyword = "transformer"
2. Call 2: keyword = "attention mechanism"

These are two separate, sequential calls — one per phrase, as instructed. Do not add extra search calls.

WHAT TO CAPTURE:
For EVERY entry returned across both calls, capture ALL available fields. Typically search-arxiv returns entries with fields such as: entry_id (arXiv URL or ID), title, authors, published (date), journal_ref (may be missing), summary/abstract, and possibly year. Extract and record:
- Normalized paper ID: derive the arXiv-style ID (e.g., "1706.03762" from URLs like http://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762v2 — strip version suffix and URL prefix). If an entry has no usable ID, note it as missing.
- Title (verbatim)
- Authors (full list as available)
- Publication year (extract from published/date field if present; else note missing)
- Journal reference (journal_ref if present, else note missing)
- Abstract (full text as returned; if missing note it)
- Query membership: which call(s) ("transformer" and/or "attention mechanism") returned this paper
- Duplicate detection: papers appearing in both queries (same normalized ID) — flag them; also flag any duplicate IDs within a single query's results.

OUTPUT / DELIVERABLE (return in your final message):
A complete structured report containing:
1. A JSON-serializable list (or dict keyed by normalized paper ID) of ALL unique papers with fields: paper_id, title, authors, year, journal_ref, abstract, queries (list of which queries matched).
2. The raw count of entries per query, and the unique count after dedup.
3. The list of duplicate IDs (appearing in both queries) and any missing-field controls (entries lacking ID / year / journal_ref / abstract).
4. Note anything unusual (e.g., entries that are not arXiv-style).

Do NOT write any files. Do NOT modify anything. This is strictly read-only: only call mcp__scholarly__search-arxiv (twice) and return findings in your final response. Be complete — do not truncate or summarize away any paper. Include the full abstract text for each paper.
Scholarly literature corpus collection

You are an academic-literature researcher (read-only) helping build a literature review corpus on transformer architectures in NLP.

GOAL: Collect paper metadata from the LOCAL ARXIV repository (via the arxiv_local MCP) by making EXACTLY TWO calls to the mcp__arxiv_local__search_papers tool:
1. Call 1: query = "transformer"
2. Call 2: query = "neural network"
Use max_results = 20 for each call (the largest safe result limit). Do not add extra search calls and do not add category filters — keep the searches broad.

STEPS:
1. Run the two searches above.
2. Combine (union) the results, deduplicating by normalized arXiv paper ID (e.g., "1706.03762"; strip any version suffix like "v2" and any URL prefix if present).
3. For EACH unique paper, download it with mcp__arxiv_local__download_paper(paper_id=...) and then read it with mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper(paper_id=...) to obtain and verify its abstract. (download_paper creates a resource; read_paper returns the markdown content including title/abstract/authors). Capture: paper_id, title, authors, publication year (from the entry if available), journal reference (if any is present in the metadata), and the abstract text.
4. Record query membership: which query/ies ("transformer" and/or "neural network") returned each paper, and flag duplicate IDs appearing in both queries.

PERSISTENCE (only if needed): The corpus is expected to be moderate (up to ~40 unique papers). If you judge the corpus large or if you want a durable record, write ONE runtime-unique JSON file to the task workspace directory:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace
Use a unique filename like arxiv_corpus_<your-choice>.json (include a timestamp/random suffix so it never collides). Structure: a dict {paper_id: {paper_id, title, authors, year, journal_ref, abstract, queries}} plus a "_meta" key with counts (per-query counts, unique count, duplicate IDs, missing-field controls). If you do NOT write a file, that is fine — just return everything inline.

OUTPUT / DELIVERABLE (return in your final message):
1. Complete list of ALL unique papers with fields: paper_id, title, authors, year, journal_ref, abstract (full text — do not truncate), queries.
2. Counts: results per query, unique papers after dedup, duplicate IDs (in both queries), and missing-field controls (papers lacking year/journal_ref/abstract).
3. If you persisted a JSON file: its full path, md5 hash, and file size. Use the terminal (mcp__terminal__run_command) with md5sum/stat to compute these if you write the file.

Constraints: You may call the arxiv_local MCP tools and terminal for read/checksum only. Do NOT write any artifact to the workspace other than the optional single runtime-unique JSON corpus file described above. Do not modify existing files. Be complete and verbatim in your report.
Local arXiv literature corpus collection

You are an external-workflow operator building a Notion knowledge-base database for a literature review on "Transformer Architectures in NLP".

CONTEXT / PRIOR WORK:
A research corpus has already been collected from two databases (Scholarly MCP search-arxiv and arxiv_local MCP search_papers), deduplicated, categorized, and emitted to a canonical runtime JSON at:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/canonical_papers.json

READ that file first. It contains:
- meta.total_unique_papers = 9
- meta.source_counts: {"Scholarly": 0, "Arxiv": 3, "Both": 6}
- papers[]: 9 unique papers, each with paper_id (e.g. "1706.03762"), title, authors (comma-separated string), year (int), journal_ref, abstract, category (one of "Architecture Design" | "Training Methods" | "Applications" | "Survey"), source (one of "Scholarly" | "Arxiv" | "Both"), in_scholarly, in_arxiv, overlap booleans.

YOUR DELIVERABLE — a Notion database titled EXACTLY "Research Paper Tracker" with this property schema:
- Title (type: title)            — the paper's title
- Paper_ID (type: rich_text)     — the arXiv-style paper ID as plain text (e.g. "1706.03762")
- Authors (type: rich_text)      — comma-separated author string from the JSON
- Year (type: number)            — integer year
- Category (type: select)        — options exactly: "Architecture Design", "Training Methods", "Applications", "Survey"
- Source (type: select)          — options exactly: "Scholarly", "Arxiv", "Both"
- Abstract_Summary (type: rich_text) — the paper's abstract text from the JSON

STEPS (use the Notion MCP tools; you own this database — no other agent will touch it):
1. Fully paginate a search (mcp__notion__API-post-search with query "Research Paper Tracker", follow start_cursor until no more results) to check whether a database with that EXACT title already exists. Also search for any parent page available in the workspace (e.g. search with empty query or a broad query) to host a new database if needed.
2. If an existing database with the exact title "Research Paper Tracker" is found: reuse it. Verify its property schema and, if needed, update it with mcp__notion__API-update-a-database so it has exactly the 7 properties/types/options above (merge, do not duplicate).
   If none exists: create the database with mcp__notion__API-create-a-database under an existing page (parent type "page_id"). If NO parent page exists at all, first create a page via mcp__notion__API-post-page (parent workspace, title "Research Paper Tracker" or similar) and create the database under that page.
3. For EACH of the 9 unique papers in canonical_papers.json: query the database (mcp__notion__API-post-database-query, paginate fully) to check whether a page with the same Paper_ID already exists. If it exists, UPDATE that page's properties (mcp__notion__API-patch-page). If not, CREATE a page in the database (mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent database_id) setting all 7 properties with correct Notion types:
   - title property: {"title": [{"text": {"content": "<title>"}}]}
   - rich_text: {"rich_text": [{"text": {"content": "<value>"}}]}
   - number: {"number": <year>}
   - select: {"select": {"name": "<option>"}} — only use the exact option names listed above.
   This must result in exactly 9 pages, one per unique Paper_ID (upsert semantics: no duplicate Paper_IDs).
4. READ BACK everything: query the database (fully paginated) and verify all 9 pages exist with correct Title, Paper_ID, Authors, Year, Category, Source, Abstract_Summary. Also verify the database schema (mcp__notion__API-retrieve-a-database). Self-correct any discrepancies before returning.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA / RECEIPT to report in your final message:
- The database_id (UUID) and its title, plus the list of the 7 properties with their types and select options.
- The full list of 9 pages: for each, page_id, Paper_ID, Title, Year, Category, Source (this is the receipt the coordinator will reconcile).
- Total page count and a note on whether any pre-existing duplicates were found/handled.
Do NOT modify or create anything outside this database. Do NOT touch the Word or Excel deliverables.
Build Notion Research Paper Tracker

You are an office-report builder producing a Word literature-review document on "Transformer Architectures in NLP".

CONTEXT / PRIOR WORK:
A research corpus has been collected from two databases (Scholarly MCP and arxiv_local MCP), deduplicated, categorized, and emitted to a canonical runtime JSON at:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/canonical_papers.json

READ that file first. It contains papers[] with 9 unique papers, each having: paper_id, title, authors (comma-separated string), year (int), journal_ref, abstract, category (one of "Architecture Design" | "Training Methods" | "Applications" | "Survey"), source (one of "Scholarly" | "Arxiv" | "Both"), overlap (bool). meta.category_counts shows: Architecture Design 1, Training Methods 6, Applications 1, Survey 1. Six papers have source "Both" (present in both databases); three have source "Arxiv" only.

Also READ the formatting guidance file:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/lit_review_template.md
(It requires: title "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP"; an Introduction explaining scope and methodology; one section per methodology category with relevant papers; for each paper title, authors, year, and brief abstract summary; a Conclusion summarizing findings and identifying gaps; group by category; highlight papers that appear in multiple databases; include publication year trends; minimum 500 words.)

YOUR DELIVERABLE — create the Word document at EXACTLY:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/Transformer_Literature_Review.docx
Use the mcp__word__* tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, add_table, etc.).

DOCUMENT STRUCTURE (follow lit_review_template.md):
1. Title (Heading level 1 or document title): "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP"
2. Introduction (Heading 2): explain the scope of the review (transformers in NLP), the methodology (two academic sources searched — scholarly with queries "transformer" and "attention mechanism"; arxiv repository with queries "transformer" and "neural network"; union + dedup by arXiv ID; keyword-based categorization into Architecture Design / Training Methods / Applications / Survey), and note 9 unique papers were collected with 6 appearing in both databases. Mention the publication year range (2012–2020).
3. One Heading-2 section per methodology category, in this order: "Architecture Design", "Training Methods", "Applications", "Survey". Under each section, for EVERY paper in that category (from canonical_papers.json), include a paragraph or entry with: the paper title (bold or as a lead-in), authors, year, and a brief description grounded in the paper's abstract (you may quote/paraphrase the abstract). Explicitly mark papers whose source is "Both" as appearing in multiple databases (e.g., "[in both databases]").
4. Conclusion (Heading 2): summarize the state of the field — the shift from recurrent/convolutional sequence models to attention-based transformers (2017 onward), the dominance of pre-training/scaling (BERT, T5, GPT-3), the continuing importance of training techniques (dropout 2012, batch normalization 2015), applications (machine translation with attention), and surveys (Efficient Transformers 2020). Identify research gaps grounded in the collected corpus: e.g., the corpus shows little coverage of efficiency/long-context concerns beyond the single survey, few Application-category papers, a gap in systematic comparisons of training recipes, and a need for more recent (post-2020) surveys and application benchmarks. Include publication year trends (most papers 2017–2020; training-method papers span 2012–2020).
The full document must be at least 500 words.

QUALITY REQUIREMENTS:
- Use proper heading levels and readable formatting (title heading, section headings, paragraphs).
- Cover ALL 9 papers exactly once, each with title, authors, year, and abstract-grounded description.
- Do not invent papers or metadata; everything must come from canonical_papers.json.
- After building, READ THE DOCUMENT BACK (mcp__word__get_document_text and mcp__word__get_document_outline) and self-correct if any paper is missing, headings are wrong, or content is malformed.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA / RECEIPT to report in your final message:
- Absolute path of the created .docx, its word count, and the outline (list of headings).
- Per category: the list of paper titles + years included (so the coordinator can reconcile against the JSON).
- Confirmation that papers with source "Both" were explicitly highlighted as appearing in multiple databases.
Write Transformer literature review docx

You are an office-report builder producing an Excel analysis workbook for a literature review on "Transformer Architectures in NLP".

CONTEXT / PRIOR WORK:
A research corpus has been collected from two databases (Scholarly MCP and arxiv_local MCP), deduplicated, categorized, and emitted to a canonical runtime JSON at:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/canonical_papers.json

READ that file first. It contains:
- papers[]: 9 unique papers, each with paper_id (e.g. "1706.03762"), title, authors (comma-separated string), year (int), category (one of "Architecture Design" | "Training Methods" | "Applications" | "Survey"), source (one of "Scholarly" | "Arxiv" | "Both"), in_scholarly (bool), in_arxiv (bool), overlap (bool).
- method_comparison[]: 4 rows, one per category, with category, paper_count, avg_year (number), key_papers (semicolon-separated titles).
- citation_matrix[]: 9 rows with paper_id, title, in_scholarly ("Yes"/"No"), in_arxiv ("Yes"/"No"), overlap ("Yes"/"No").

YOUR DELIVERABLE — create the Excel file at EXACTLY:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx
Use the mcp__excel__* tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet, rename_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, format_range, etc.). The workbook must have EXACTLY three sheets with EXACTLY these names and columns:

Sheet 1 — "Paper_Catalog": columns Paper_ID | Title | Authors | Year | Source | Category
  - One row per unique paper (9 rows), ordered as in canonical_papers.json papers[].
  - Source values: "Scholarly", "Arxiv", or "Both" (from the JSON source field). Category values exactly as in the JSON.

Sheet 2 — "Method_Comparison": columns Category | Paper_Count | Avg_Year | Key_Papers
  - One row per category (4 rows), using method_comparison[] from the JSON (Avg_Year as the number, e.g. 2016.2; Key_Papers as the semicolon-separated title string).

Sheet 3 — "Citation_Matrix": columns Paper_ID | Title | In_Scholarly | In_Arxiv | Overlap
  - One row per unique paper (9 rows), using citation_matrix[] from the JSON ("Yes"/"No" strings).

CRITICAL FORMATTING RULES:
- Write paper IDs as PLAIN TEXT (e.g. 1706.03762, 1207.00580) — never as formulas, never with leading apostrophe tricks that alter the value; keep the literal string.
- Write ALL other cell values as LITERAL values (numbers as numbers, text as text). Do NOT write any Excel formulas (=...), do not use apply_formula.
- You may format headers (bold, background) for readability, but do not change any values.

PROCEDURE:
1. Create the workbook (mcp__excel__create_workbook), then ensure exactly three worksheets with the exact names above (create/rename/delete as needed so no extra default sheets remain).
2. Populate each sheet with header row + data rows via mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel.
3. READ BACK all populated ranges (mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel for each sheet, full range) and verify: 9 data rows + header in Paper_Catalog and Citation_Matrix; 4 data rows + header in Method_Comparison; all IDs are literal text; all Source/Category/Yes-No values match the JSON. Self-correct any mismatch before returning (e.g., fix stray sheets, wrong values).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA / RECEIPT to report in your final message:
- Absolute path of the created .xlsx and the sheet names present.
- For each sheet: the populated range (e.g. A1:F10) and a compact dump of its contents (IDs, titles, counts) so the coordinator can reconcile against the JSON.
- Explicit confirmation that no formulas were used and IDs are plain text.
